newsitem.title: USA: ESS Technology sees Q2 below expecations.
newsitem.headline: ESS Technology sees Q2 below expecations.

text.p: FREMONT, Calif., June 13 - ESS Technology Inc said Thursday night it expected second quarter revenues to grow at a lower than expected 22 percent compared to second quarter last year because of softer than anticipated seasonal demand for audio products, especially in the add-in sound card market, and competitive pricing pressures in the audio and video CD markets.

The company said it expected net sales for the second quarter, ending June 30, 1997, to be between $56 and $61 million and earnings between to be $0.16 and $0.19 per share before a one-time charge of $0.64 per share resulting from the acquisition of Platform Technologies Inc for 2.54 million shares of ESS common stock.
ESS earned $0.28 per share in the second quarter of 1996.
On Thursday, the company announced the completion of the previously announced Platform acquisition.

"We anticipated this quarter might be difficult, because of historic slow seasonal demand and competitive price pressure and because it is a transition quarter to our new products for the second half of the year," said chief executive Fred Chan.

"We are optimistic about the impact of our new products going forward. All of our lines, including audio, video and communications, have new products in production that will begin shipping in June," Chan said.
